subject.title: [RFC] Context Provenance: Add source/volatility metadata to injected context segments

question: Should OpenClaw adopt model-visible inline provenance tags for injected context segments, or should provenance/freshness be carried through a runtime-owned context-engine contract instead?
rationale: Current main lacks the requested behavior, but the RFC changes core prompt shape and may affect cache stability, session-state semantics, memory output, and future config surface, so automation should not pick the permanent design.

options.title: Review and narrow Phase 1
options.body: Use the open Phase 1 PR as the candidate, but require maintainers to settle the inline tag format and proof expectations before merge.

options.title: Move to runtime-owned provenance
options.body: Reject inline prompt tags for now and pursue structured context-engine or runtime metadata like the adjacent InputProvenance discussion.

options.title: Decline this direction
options.body: Close the RFC and linked PR if maintainers decide the token/prompt-cache cost and model-compliance reliance are not worth adding to core.

recommendation.title: Review and narrow Phase 1
recommendation.body: Use the open Phase 1 PR as the candidate, but require maintainers to settle the inline tag format and proof expectations before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent has recent prompt-cache and stable-context ownership in the exact area affected by inline provenance tags.
